subject: Economics
description: RBI tools, SLR, CRR, repo rate, types of accounts

questions.stem: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank of the country, was established in:
questions.explanation: The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (1926). Initially a private shareholders' bank; nationalised on 1 January 1949. First Governor — Sir Osborne Smith; first Indian Governor — Sir C. D. Deshmukh (1943-49). Headquarters — originally Kolkata, now Mumbai (since 1937).

questions.stem: The 'Repo Rate' set by the RBI is the rate at which:

options.option_text: Commercial banks lend to the RBI
The RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks
Banks charge customers for savings accounts

questions.explanation: Repo ('repurchase') rate — RBI lends short-term (1-day) money to banks against collateral (government securities); 'repo' means the bank agrees to repurchase the securities at a higher price. Reverse repo rate — banks park surplus cash with RBI; lower than repo. Bank Rate — longer-term RBI lending, largely symbolic now. MSF — marginal standing facility, slightly above repo.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The proportion of a bank's deposits that it must keep as cash with the RBI (not earning interest) is called the:
questions.explanation: CRR — cash the bank must hold with the RBI, in proportion to its NDTL. SLR — additional liquid assets (cash, gold or approved govt. securities) held with the bank itself. Both tighten / loosen the money supply. Raising CRR pulls liquidity out, cooling inflation; cutting CRR releases funds, supporting growth. Interest-free; currently around 4.5 % (SLR ~18 %).

questions.stem: The largest public-sector bank in India by asset size is:
questions.explanation: SBI — largest commercial bank in India by assets, deposits, branches and customer base. Successor to the Imperial Bank of India (1921). Nationalised in 1955. In 2017 it merged with its five associate banks (State Bank of Mysore / Hyderabad / Travancore / Patiala / Bikaner & Jaipur) + Bharatiya Mahila Bank. PNB, BoB and Canara are the next-largest PSBs after the bank-consolidation of 2019-20.

questions.stem: Nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks in India took place in:
questions.explanation: 14 commercial banks with deposits above ₹50 crore were nationalised by Indira Gandhi's government in July 1969. Six more banks were nationalised in 1980 (bringing the total to 20). 1956 — SBI was nationalised. 1991 — LPG reforms allowed new private banks (ICICI, HDFC, Axis, IndusInd) to enter.

questions.stem: In banking terminology, an 'NPA' (Non-Performing Asset) is a loan on which principal or interest repayments are overdue for:
questions.explanation: RBI classifies a loan as an NPA once dues are overdue for more than 90 days. Further categories — Sub-standard (NPA up to 12 months), Doubtful (NPA over 12 months), Loss (unrecoverable). Indian banks' GNPA ratio peaked at ~11.5 % in 2018 and has since fallen sharply, helped by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC 2016) and the Bad Bank (NARCL 2021).

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the Reserve Bank of India?

options.option_text: Acting as banker to the Government

questions.explanation: Direct taxes (income-tax, corporate tax) are collected by the CBDT; indirect taxes (GST, customs) by the CBIC — both under the Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance. The RBI's functions include currency issuance (notes of ₹2 and above — ₹1 notes are by the Finance Ministry), banker to Government and banks, monetary policy (repo, CRR), foreign-exchange management, consumer protection, macro-prudential regulation.
